newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOWE-GOLOTA REMATCH WILL BE UNDER HEAVY SECURITY.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOWE-GOLOTA REMATCH WILL BE UNDER HEAVY SECURITY.

text.p: In a bid to ensure only Riddick Bowe and Andrew Golota will do the fighting in their rematch on Saturday, promoters will beef up security inside the Atlancit City Convention Centre.

The two heavyweights' first bout July 11 at Madison Square Garden ended in chaos. Fights inside the ring between members of the oppossing camps and outside the ring between rival fans erupted after Bowe, 39-1, was declared the winner when Golota, 28-1,was disqualified for low blows in the seventh round.
There were handfuls of arrests and injuries in the melee, including one suffered by the Polish-born Golota when he was struck on the head by a walkie talkie wielded by a member of Bowe's camp.

"Let me say this to you very emphatically, I can not emphasise this enough, I will be carried out of this arena on a stretcher before I allow something like that to happen in New Jersey," said New Jersey boxing commissioner Larry Hazzard at a news conference Wednesday.

"We feel very confident that there will not even be a trace of a problem Saturday night," said promoter Dino Duva. "This thing will be settled one way Saturday night in the ring with the two fighters, and only the two fighters alone."

Rich Rose, an executive of Caesars, which is involved in promoting the fight, said: "We have done a lot of big fights here, (Evander) Holyfield-Foreman, (Mike) Tyson-(Michael) Spinks and it has never been a problem here."
Just to make sure, extra precautions have been taken.
"I wasn't that concerned about anything happening, but we thought the right thing to do just from a perception standpoint was to beef up security to act as a deterrent," Duva said.
According to Duva, there will be more than 100 security personnel, including 50-75 policemen augmenting the arena's own security force, inside the 12,000-seat Convention Centre.
"There will be about 25 cops ringside, and usually there are six or eight for big fights," said Duva.
Duva said the number of people with access to the ring has been severely reduced.

"We made this a condition of making the fight, to strictly limit the ringside credentials," said Duva. "Both camps, are limited to eight credentials and only four of them will be allowed in the ring."
In the first fight, members of Bowe's camp jumped into the ring and started throwing punches at Golota.
"I heard at the Garden that the Bowe camp had as many as 75 to 100 credentials which is ridiculous," said Duva. "Normally on a big heavyweight fight,the number is about 20 on each side."
Bowe's promoter Rock Newman had been a ligthening rod for blame over the fracas, leading the charge across the ring at Golota.
But Newman offered no remorse for his behaviour.

"I only did what I was authorised and credentialed to do," Newman said. "I screamed at Golota which is no offence whatsoever and immediately knelt down and picked Bowe up and all hell broke loose as my back was to the action. That is what they found."
But Duva thinks Newman "deep down knows he made a mistake and I truly believe that Rock is not going to cause trouble in the ring Saturday," said Duva.
